scene.head: with_body
scene.placeText: the seaside line of the brass-trimmed steam tram of her steam city on a bright afternoon — the little open tram puffing clean white steam along the harbour quay, passengers on its polished wooden benches, gas lamps along the rails, paddle-steamers at the piers and the green hills of the hot-spring town ahead
scene.ownProp: a small polished brass conductor's hand bell on a turned wooden handle, a camellia-red silk tassel swinging from it
scene.outfit: a tram-conductor look fitted to her body — a sleeveless harbour-blue waistcoat with polished brass buttons over a lace-edged camisole, high-waisted shorts, a sash strung with brass tram tokens, a slim belt with a brass ticket punch, fine leather gloves, laced ankle boots, a little round conductor's cap with a steam-tram badge and a red camellia at her collar
scene.scene: she is the conductor of the steam tram to the hot-spring town, striding along the tram's running board and ringing her brass hand bell to call the next stop

prompt:

She is strikingly beautiful and refined — harmonious features, clear luminous skin, graceful posture — while her own face stays distinct: her face shape, eyes, brows, nose and lips follow the attached image, not a generic pretty face.

This is her world's own everyday life, not our present day: every made thing around her — tools, cups, lamps, signs, vehicles, money and devices — is made the way her world makes them.
Let the place itself carry this world through its materials, fittings and objects; do not add the city's landmarks, airships or a skyline unless the place below names them. Wherever the place below sounds sooty, smoky, grimy or rusty, show it clean and gleaming instead.
